question.prompt: How many integers between \(2020\) and \(2400\) have four distinct digits arranged in increasing order? (For example, \(2357\) is one such integer.)

solutions.explanation:
The first digit must be \(2\), because the number lies between \(2020\) and \(2400\). Increasing digits force the second digit to be greater than \(2\); it must be \(3\), since a second digit of \(4\) or more would put the number above \(2400\).

The number therefore begins with \(23\). Count by its third digit:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{Third digit}&\text{Choices for the last digit}\\\hline
4&5,6,7,8,9\\
5&6,7,8,9\\
6&7,8,9\\
7&8,9\\
8&9
\end{array}
\]

There are \(5+4+3+2+1=\boxed{15}\) numbers, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\). Each is counted once by its third digit, and every listed ending is strictly increasing.
solutions.title: Fix the first two digits and count increasing endings
